comparison: Perfect match on Mgm1 localization claims (C38-C42). Both evaluations find the data SUPPORTED. OpenEval notes the quantitative immuno-EM and fractionation data provide important mechanistic context. Peer reviewers accept the localization findings without challenge, though they request discussion of whether Mgm1 affects inner membrane morphology independently of its fusion role.

Strong match on conservation claims (C121-C129, with C8 only in OpenEval). Both evaluations find these claims SUPPORTED. Both note these are based on published literature and citations. OpenEval emphasizes the conservation argument strengthens general applicability despite limited direct experimental evidence in yeast. Peer reviewers acknowledge conservation of key components in structure and function throughout evolution.

Substantial overlap on Mgm1's direct role in cristae formation (C3, C30, C33, C36, C37, C108, C109). OpenEval finds all claims SUPPORTED with strong experimental evidence from temperature-shift experiments. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, explicitly affirming the direct involvement of Mgm1 and calling it 'novel and very interesting.' Both highlight the rapid reversibility as an important finding.

Partial overlap on maintenance of mtDNA and respiratory complexes during crista loss (C31, C34, C111). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED, noting they strengthen the conclusion of a direct role. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, raising significant mechanistic questions about how cristae can disappear so quickly without degradation of respiratory chain complexes or ATPases. This represents a key disagreement in interpretation.

Strong overlap on F1FO ATP synthase dimerization and cristae formation (C43-C50, C52, C53, plus C6-C7 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, though notes the inference about dimeric F1FO assembly is somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, questioning whether dimeric ATP synthase is strictly required for all cristae versus just tubular cristae, and requesting additional experiments to test the hypothesis.

Strong overlap on MICOS role and protein distributions (C54-C62, C68, plus C64-C66 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED but notes the conclusion about functional similarity may be overstated. Peer reviewers mark this UNCERTAIN, challenging the interpretation that MICOS is strictly required for cristae biogenesis versus crista junction maintenance, noting that MICOS mutants still contain cristae-like structures.

Partial overlap on MICOS dissociation and insufficiency (C63-C66, C69). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED though notes inferences are somewhat speculative. Peer reviewers mark related claims UNCERTAIN, questioning MICOS's precise role and whether it's required for cristae biogenesis or just crista junction maintenance. Both acknowledge the data quality but differ on mechanistic interpretation.

Moderate overlap on MICOS overexpression effects and two-pathway model support (C72, C74, C78-C80, plus C88-C92, C102-C104 in peer review). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED with reasonable inferences from correlation data. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, acknowledging the data supports the two-pathway model, though they request discussion of potential secondary effects and suggest temperature-sensitive mutants could strengthen conclusions.

Partial overlap on electron tomography findings (C75-C77). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED as part of MICOS overexpression analysis. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED as part of their evaluation of tubular cristae prevalence in Mgm1-reduced conditions, explicitly praising the electron cryo-tomography technology enabling this finding.

Partial overlap on tubular cristae in double mutants (C84-C86). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting this represents strong evidence for the central two-pathway hypothesis. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, explicitly stating the data 'clearly support...the strong prevalence of tubular cristae in mitochondria with reduced Mgm1 activity' and identifying this as an important new finding.

Partial overlap on two-pathway model conclusions (C5, C102, C103). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting this represents the central hypothesis of the paper with strong support from multiple mutants. Peer reviewers also find related claims SUPPORTED, acknowledging the two-pathway model is supported by the data, though requesting discussion of potential secondary effects.

Moderate overlap on systematic mutant analysis supporting two-pathway model (C88-C92, C104). OpenEval finds claims SUPPORTED, noting the systematic analysis provides strong support for the two-pathway model. Peer reviewers also find this SUPPORTED, accepting the data as high quality and carefully conducted, though requesting discussion of potential secondary effects from steady-state depletion.

Overlap on summary claims about F1FO dimerization and MICOS requirements (C6, C7). OpenEval finds these summary claims SUPPORTED by extensive mutant analysis. Peer reviewers mark related detailed claims UNCERTAIN, questioning whether dimeric ATP synthase is strictly required for all cristae and requesting additional experiments. This shows agreement on data quality but disagreement on mechanistic interpretation.

Partial overlap on prior published work context (C105-C107). OpenEval finds these claims SUPPORTED as important context from prior work. Peer reviewers also find these background claims SUPPORTED, noting they are based on published literature and provide context for interpreting novel findings. Full agreement on these contextual claims.

Partial overlap on mechanistic background from literature (C112-C115). OpenEval finds all claims C112-C120 SUPPORTED by citations, providing mechanistic context. Peer reviewers also find these background claims SUPPORTED without challenge. Both evaluations agree these represent prior work providing important context rather than novel discoveries.

OpenEval evaluates foundational background knowledge about mitochondrial structure (C1, C2, C9-C22) as SUPPORTED by citations and standard structural descriptions. No corresponding peer review evaluation found for these specific background claims, though peer reviewers implicitly accept this foundational knowledge in their evaluations of novel findings.
